body_ar:
من هم أهل الكلام وماذا تعنون بهم؟

أهل الكلام اسم اشتهر إطلاقه على طائفة من هذه الأمة وضعت قواعد لضوابط العقول، وذلك أن الشارع أحال علم بعض الأمور على العقل وعلوم الناس متفاوتة متباينة، ولا يمكن أن يجعل واحد منها حجة على باقيها، فاحتيج إلى وضع معايير وضوابط يرجع إليها الناس عند تخالف عقولهم

وأنتم تعلمون أن توزيع الله سبحانه وتعالى للعقول بين الناس متباين، ولذلك يقول الحكماء: ما من أحد إلا وهو راض عن الله في عقله، وأقلهم عقلا أرضاهم به، أقل الناس نصيبا من العقل يظن أنه أعقل الناس، وهذا من حكمة الله تعالى ولطفه، فكيف يتحاكم إلى هذا العقل الذي يتفاوت الناس فيه لا بد من وضع ضوابط يرجع إليها،

وهذه الضوابط هي التي سميت بالحجج والبراهين وبالقضايا التي هي الدعاوي، ومبناها على التفريق بين التصديق والتصور، فالتصور هو إدراك المفرد والتصديق هو إدراك النسبة أي إثبات أمر لأمر أو نفيه عنه،

وهذه القواعد العقلية هي من الاجتهاد المحض، ولا يمكن أن تكون خطأ مائة بالمائة ولا صوابا مائة بالمائة، وقد حصل الخطأ في كثير من جوانبها وبالأخص حين ترجمت إليها نظريات اليونان الإغريق ونظريات الرومان، ولا شك أن نظريات هذه الأمم السابقة يخالطها كثير من الوثنيات والشركيات،

وكذلك فإن كثيرا من الذين درسوا علم الكلام وتعمقوا في هذه القواعد غلوا في العقل حتى أخرجوه عن طوره، والعقل جارحة من جوارح الإنسان فهو مثل عينه وأذنه ويده ولا يمكن الغلو فيه لأن له حدودا إلى أعلى وحدودا إلى أسفل، فحدوده إلى أسفل هي الأوليات والمشاهدات والحدسيات والمحسوسات والمشهورات فهذه هي الحد الأدنى للعقل والسقف الأعلى له هي مواقف العقول التسعة التي يجمعها قوله: عجل وقتب، فالعين للعرو من النقيضين، والجيم لجمعهما، واللام للزوم الدور أوالتسلسل والواو لوقوع عدد لا نهاية له، والقاف لقلب الحقيقة، والتاء لتعدد الفاعل وتحصيل الحاصل وكذلك لترجيح بلا مرجح، والباء لبطلان الحصر،

فهذه تسعة هي مواقف العقول التي تقف عندها فإذا كانت العقول كذلك فلا يمكن أن نغلو فيها أو نجعلها يتحاكم إليها في كل الأمور بل الحكم للشخص هو خطاب الله لا خطاب العقل،

ومن هنا فإن كثيرا من المتكلمين يغلطون في تصور العقل، ولذلك قال الغزالي رحمه الله: الوحي عقل من الخارج والعقل وحي من الداخل، ولا شك أن هذا من الغلو في العقل، لأن العقل الذي يتكلم عنه الغزالي ليس متمثلا في عقل شخص بعينه، فلا يقصد عقل أبي حامد الغزالي مثلا، أو عقل إنسان بعينه،بل يقصد الوجود المطلق الذي هو الوجود الذهني للعقل، ولا يقصد الوجود الخارجي المتمثل في عقل شخص من الأشخاص أو جماعة من الجماعات، وإذا كان الحكم على ماهية ذهنية غير خارجية فهو حكم غير دقيق،

كذلك فإن مما خالط ما يسمى بعلم الكلام الخوض في صفات الله تعالى بغير علم، وهذا من الخطر الماحق، لأن الله تعالى: {لَا تُدْرِكُهُ الْأَبْصَارُ وَهُوَ يُدْرِكُ الْأَبْصَارَ وَهُوَ اللَّطِيفُ الْخَبِيرُ (103)} [الأنعام] وقد ذكرنا في الدرس الماضي أنه لا يمكن أن يثبت له إلا ما أثبته لنفسه أو أثبته له رسوله (ص) فلا يمكن أن يصل علم الحادث إليه، بل لا يمكن أن يعلم عنه إلا ما أوحى به، وإذا كان الأمر كذلك فلا مجال للعقل في هذا الباب،

وأهل الكلام فرق كثيرة دخلت علوما متعددة، ففي علوم اللغة طائفة متكلمة وهي التي تسمى بأهل التقعيد العقلي وهم أهل الكوفة، فأهل الكوفة مثلا إذا وجدوا أي نادرة لغوية قاسوا عليها وجعلوها قاعدة، وأهل البصرة يضعون قاعدة بالأكثرية وما خالفها جعلوه من الشواذ، أو بحثوا له عن تأويل يرده إلى القاعدة الأصلية، مثل خلافهم في تقدم الفاعل، فإن أهل البصرة يقولون الفاعل لا يتقدم: وبعد فعل فاعل فإن ظهر** فهو وإلا فضمير استتر لكن الكوفيين يقولون لا، بل يوجد فاعل متقدم، والبصريون يقولون: إذا وجد فإنه فاعل فعل محذوف يدل عليه ما بعده،

وكذلك في الأصول، ففي الأصول مدرسة تسمى المدرسة الكلامية وهي التي تبني القواعد الأصولية وقواعد الاستنباط واستغلال النصوص الشرعية على مقتضى القوانين العقلية، وهذه المدرسة هي التي سلكت في المذاهب الثلاثة المذهب المالكي والمذهب الشافعي والمذهب الحنبلي، وخالفتها مدرسة تسمى مدرسة الفقهاء وهي مدرسة الحنفية، فإنهم اعتمدوا على التفريع الفقهي ولم يعتمدوا على ترتيب المقدمات المنطقية العقلية،

وكذلك دخل هذا العلم في علم العقائد ووضع فيه كثير من الكتب واشتهر كثير من الفرق الداخلة في مسمى الكلام، مثل الكَلَّابية أصحاب ابن كَلَّاب، والكَرَّامية أصحاب ابن كَرَّام، وكذلك إلى حد ما الماتُريدِيَة والأشعرية أي أتباع هذين الإمامين، فكثير منهم أيضا دخلوا في علم الكلام وتوغلوا فيه،

وكذلك في التفسير فإن بعض المفسرين يدخلون في مسمى أهل الكلام لانشغالهم بالتفسير العقلي بالرأي المحض، ومن ذلك التفسير الإشاري الذي اشتغل به الألوسي رحمه الله تعالى وأدرجه في آخر تفسير كل آية من تفسيره تقريبا.
body_en:
Who are the people of kalām, and what do you mean by them?

'The people of kalām' is a name that has become well known as applied to a group of this community who laid down rules for the standards that govern the intellect. That is because the Lawgiver referred knowledge of some matters to the intellect, while people's understandings are disparate and divergent, and it is not possible to make any one of them a proof against the rest. So there was a need to lay down criteria and controls to which people could refer when their intellects diverge.

You know that God's distribution of intellects among people is uneven. That is why the sages say: there is no one who is not content with God as regards his own intellect, and those with the least intellect are the most content with it. The person with the smallest share of intellect thinks he is the most intelligent of people — and this is part of God's wisdom, exalted, and His kindness. So how can judgement be referred to this intellect, in which people vary? Controls must be laid down to which reference can be made.

These controls are what are called the proofs and the demonstrations, and the propositions, which are the claims. Their basis is the distinction between assent (taṣdīq) and conception (taṣawwur): conception is the grasping of a single notion, and assent is the grasping of a relation — that is, the affirming of one thing of another, or the denying of it.

These rational rules are pure exercise of reasoning; they cannot be a hundred per cent wrong, nor a hundred per cent right. Error has occurred in many of their aspects, and especially when the theories of the Greeks and the theories of the Romans were translated into them; and there is no doubt that the theories of these earlier nations are mixed with much that is pagan and much that associates partners with God.

Likewise, many of those who studied the science of kalām and went deep into these rules went to excess concerning the intellect, until they took it out of its proper bounds. The intellect is one of the faculties of the human being; it is like his eye, his ear and his hand, and there can be no going to excess in it, because it has limits at the upper end and limits at the lower end. Its limits at the lower end are the primary truths, the observed, the intuited, the sensed and the widely held — these are the lower bound of the intellect. Its upper ceiling is the nine points at which intellects come to a halt, which are gathered in the phrase 'ʿajil wa-qatab': the ʿayn is for the absence of both contradictories; the jīm is for joining the two together; the lām is for the necessity of circularity or of infinite regress; the wāw is for the occurrence of a number without end; the qāf is for the reversal of a reality; the tāʾ is for the multiplicity of the agent, and for the obtaining of what already obtains, and likewise for preponderance without a preponderating factor; and the bāʾ is for the collapse of an exhaustive division.

These are nine: they are the points at which intellects come to a halt. And if intellects are like this, then we cannot go to excess concerning them, nor make them the thing to which judgement is referred in all matters. Rather, the ruling upon a person is God's address, not the address of the intellect.

From here, many of the theologians err in how they conceive the intellect. That is why al-Ghazali, may God have mercy on him, said: revelation is an intellect from without, and the intellect is a revelation from within. There is no doubt that this is part of going to excess concerning the intellect, because the intellect al-Ghazali is speaking of is not embodied in the intellect of any particular person — he does not mean the intellect of Abu Hamid al-Ghazali, for instance, or the intellect of a particular human being; rather he means absolute existence, which is the mental existence of the intellect, and he does not mean external existence, embodied in the intellect of one person among persons or one group among groups. And when a judgement is passed on a mental quiddity rather than an external one, it is not a precise judgement.

Likewise, part of what has become mixed into what is called the science of kalām is plunging into the attributes of God, exalted, without knowledge — and this is an obliterating danger, because God, exalted: {Vision does not grasp Him, and He grasps vision; and He is the Subtle, the Aware (103)} [الأنعام] (Sūrat al-Anʿām 6:103). We mentioned in the previous lesson that nothing can be affirmed of Him except what He has affirmed of Himself, or what His Messenger, upon whom be peace, affirmed of Him; so the knowledge of an originated being cannot reach Him — indeed nothing can be known about Him except what He has revealed. And if the matter is so, then there is no scope for the intellect in this chapter.

The people of kalām are many groups, and they entered a number of sciences. In the language sciences there is a theologising faction, the one called the people of rational rule-making, and they are the people of Kufa. The people of Kufa, for instance, when they find any rare linguistic form, draw an analogy upon it and make it a rule; whereas the people of Basra lay down a rule by the majority usage, and whatever contradicts it they treat as anomalous, or else they seek an interpretation of it that returns it to the original rule. An example is their disagreement over whether the agent may precede. The people of Basra say the agent does not precede: *and after a verb comes an agent; if it appears, that is it, and otherwise a pronoun lies concealed.* But the Kufans say no, a preceding agent does exist; and the Basrans say that where such a thing is found, it is the agent of an omitted verb indicated by what comes after it.

Likewise in legal theory (uṣūl al-fiqh). In legal theory there is a school called the theological school, which builds the principles of legal theory, and the rules of derivation and of drawing on the texts of the revealed law, upon what the laws of the intellect require. This is the school that was followed in three of the schools of law — the Maliki, the Shafi'i and the Hanbali — and opposed to it is a school called the school of the jurists, which is the school of the Hanafis, for they relied upon the ramification of legal cases and did not rely upon the arranging of rational, logical premises.

Likewise this science entered the science of creed, and many books were composed in it, and many groups falling under the name of kalām became well known — such as the Kullabiyyah, the followers of Ibn Kullab; the Karramiyyah, the followers of Ibn Karram; and likewise, to a degree, the Maturidiyyah and the Ashariyyah, that is, the followers of these two imams, for many of them too entered the science of kalām and went far into it.

Likewise in exegesis: some of the exegetes fall under the name of the people of kalām, because of their occupation with rational exegesis by pure opinion. Of that is the allusive exegesis which al-Alusi, may God have mercy on him, occupied himself with, and which he appended at the end of his exegesis of almost every verse.

flags.arabic: مواقف العقول التسعة التي يجمعها قوله: عجل وقتب
flags.context: the mnemonic and the nine impossibilities it encodes
options: keep the Arabic mnemonic transliterated and translate each of the nine, as done here
translate the nine and drop the mnemonic, which does not work in English
keep the mnemonic and give the nine in a note
flags.note: The mnemonic ʿajil wa-qatab works only in Arabic: each consonant is the first letter of one of the nine impossibilities, and the tāʾ carries three of them, which is how seven letters yield nine items. The English keeps the letters so the structure is visible, but a reader without Arabic will not see why the letters are those letters. The list itself is the standard one of the logicians: the two contradictories both false, the two contradictories both true, circularity or infinite regress, an actual infinite, the reversal of a thing's reality, two agents for one effect, the obtaining of what already obtains, preponderance without a preponderating factor, and the failure of an exhaustive division.

options: the removal of the two contradictories
flags.note: العُرُوّ (from عري, to be bare) here means that neither of two contradictories holds — the technical impossibility usually named as الخلو من النقيضين, 'the vacating of both contradictories', paired with the jīm which is their conjunction. 'Removal' would suggest an act performed on them rather than a state of affairs.

flags.arabic: الوحي عقل من الخارج والعقل وحي من الداخل
flags.context: ولذلك قال الغزالي رحمه الله: الوحي عقل من الخارج والعقل وحي من الداخل
options: revelation is an intellect from without, and the intellect is a revelation from within
revelation is reason coming from outside, and reason is revelation coming from inside
revelation is an external intellect, and the intellect an internal revelation
flags.note: A well-known epigram attributed to al-Ghazali, which the Sheikh quotes in order to criticise it. The attribution is his; he gives no source, and none has been supplied. The symmetry of the Arabic is the point of the sentence and has been kept.

translator_notes: Qur'anic renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.
The source supplies its own sura marker and verse number for the Qur'anic quotation ('[الأنعام]' with '(103)' inside the braces). Those have been kept and the full house reference added beside them.

The Sheikh refers back to 'the previous lesson' on what may be affirmed of God. The cross-reference is his; the lesson referred to is not on this page and nothing has been supplied for it. This indicates the piece is part of a course rather than a standalone fatwa.

He is describing the people of kalām critically but not condemning them wholesale: he says their rules are 'pure exercise of reasoning' which can be 'neither a hundred per cent wrong nor a hundred per cent right'. That balance has been kept exactly, and not tipped either way.

Note for a later reviser: the terms wājib, jāʾiz and mumtaniʿ do not occur in this file, but its subject matter is the very context in which style guide §8 applies. If those words are introduced into any summary or heading for this article, they must take the kalām senses, not the five legal rulings.
